subject: Private deployment capacity sanity + network ops checklist for Acme
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment capacity sanity + network ops checklist for Acme

Team — I put together a short draft of sizing for Acme's private GPU pool and a companion network checklist. High-level goals from the kickoff: sustained throughput ~300k tokens/min (aggregate), 99th pct latency target <= 250ms for 8k-context gen paths, and predictable headroom for burst windows (6x sustained for 3m).

What I've attached: acme-capacity-calcs-v3.xlsx (baseline math, per-pod throughput, admission thresholds) and network-crossconnect-checklist.md (peering, cross-connect, NIC oversubscription guardrails). Key assumptions are in the first tab of the sheet. TL;DR numbers:
- Baseline node (A100x2-ish perf) estimates 10k tokens/min sustained at median 512-token seq per request (with our quant path);
- We recommend 32 nodes carved as a private pool to meet 300k sustained with 1.25x buffer (i.e., 40 nodes live) and a 2-stage burst policy (warm pool + on-demand carve);
- Admission policy: soft queueing to 60s, aggressive prefix/KV caching for repeat sessions, fallback variant (smaller model) if headroom breached.

Requests / asks:
1) Karthik — sanity-check the admission math and the 10k tokens/min per-node baseline (I used your perf table from Aug).
2) Marissa — can you validate SLA language we should pre-commit for the canary (especially fallback model behavior and failover region)?
3) Laura — network: confirm egress envelopes and whether 40 nodes is realistic for their private VPC cross-connect (I flagged an egress cap at 50Gbps in the sheet).

If this aligns I want to sync with Acme this afternoon and share the calc + a one-page runbook for cutover.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme-capacity-calcs-v3.xlsx, network-crossconnect-checklist.md
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity sanity + network ops checklist for Acme

Jonas — quick read; good work. Two quick notes inline: 

- Per-node baseline: my lab runs on A100x2 with our quant path show ~11.2k tokens/min median for 512-seq if we allow continuous batching; 10k is conservative and fine for contractual math. I flagged the sheet with an alternate-perf column for 11.2k.
- Burst policy: the 6x headroom for 3m is fine but we should explicitly specify warm-pool warmup time and cache-warm policy. If warm pool nodes take ~45s to warm, we should plan an earlier prefilling window for scheduled events.
- Admission: prefer hard admission at 120s (not 60s) for this customer; they tolerate longer queues for better cost predictability. Suggest soft queue action at 45s to return informative 429/Retry-After.

Operational asks:
1) Add a new calc tab that shows cost delta between 32 live / 40 reserved / 48 reserved (simple monthly).
2) Add a short note on model fallback quality delta — what prompt sets degrade and by how much. Marissa, can your team produce a 3–5 prompt smoke test?

If these changes are ok I can run a micro-sim later today and post a short chart.

-Karthik

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the draft — this is helpful. A few clarifying Qs from my side before we commit to a slot on Friday's cutover window: 

1) Sustained throughput: our internal traffic engineering team measured ~250k tokens/min during peak for current prod; you have 300k target. Can you confirm the margin (300k vs our 250k) and the expected tail risk if we run sustained spikes of 500k for <2m?
2) Egress: our colo team prefers a 100Gbps cross-connect. Your sheet references a 50Gbps envelope; will that throttle our peak?
3) SLA and fallbacks: procurement asked whether Redwood will maintain the 99th pct latency target if we allow fallback to smaller models — or is that only guaranteed on the primary model? We also need an outline of the canary rollback steps for infra/network reasons.

We'd like the one-page cutover runbook and a concise cost delta (32 vs 40 vs 48 nodes) before we sign the reservation addendum. Can you also add the network contact and a preferred PoC (we'll loop in colo for cross-connect provisioning).

Happy to hop on a 30m call this afternoon at 3pm PST if that helps.

—Sara

Sara / Acme team — thanks for the quick feedback. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Margin & spikes: 300k is our recommended committed sustained target with the proposed 1.25x buffer. For very short spikes (<=2m) the warm-pool + admission policy will absorb up to ~500k tokens/min with increased tail latency; beyond that we will trigger fallback model routing. I've added a micro-sim sheet (Drive link below) showing expected 99/95/50pct curves for the 32/40/48 node configs.

2) Egress: if you can provision 100Gbps cross-connect that's ideal — it eliminates the 50Gbps cap we used for conservative math. With 100Gbps the 40-node reserve comfortably covers the 500k transient spikes for the 3m window. Laura: please start the cross-connect readiness checklist with Acme's colo contact.

3) SLA + fallbacks: SLA guarantees (99th pct latency) apply to the primary model when running within the contracted capacity envelope. If we intentionally route to a fallback smaller model during overload, latency numbers may improve but quality delta will vary. We'll commit to the canary rollback steps in the one-page runbook and include an explicit quality-regression threshold that will gate an automatic rollback (suggested metric: top-line prompt-set rouge rate > 3%). Marissa — can your team draft the 3–5 prompt smoke tests and the quality-regression note?

Attachments/links: one-page runbook (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bAcmeCapacityDocs
JIRA ticket (provisioning tracker): JIRA-OPS-9812

Next steps:
- Laura to own cross-connect coordination (action: start ticket today)
- Karthik to finalize admission delta and populate alternate perf column
- Marissa to supply prompt smoke tests and quality regression note by EOD tomorrow
- I'll send the cost delta and the edited calc sheet by 5pm PST today.

I'll take the 3pm PST call if you confirm; otherwise we'll push to 10am Monday.

Thanks — Jonas
